scope: Author-stated unperformed proposals in the discrete-optics sources most directly matching the current cosine-band wavepacket model; bounded follow-up check.

sources.title: Discrete diffraction and shape-invariant beams in optical waveguide arrays
read_locations: PDF p.12, Section IV.B immediately before Conclusions
sources.assessment: Conclusions summarize completed moment laws, self-collimation, discrete Bessel beams, beam tilting, self-imaging and polygonal Bloch oscillations. No explicit unresolved future program is stated. The separable two-dimensional extension is already given in Eqs.91-94, so it is not a future-work gap.

sources.title: The peculiarities of discrete diffraction in two-dimensional optical waveguide arrays
read_locations: PDF p.4, final scientific paragraph and Conclusion
sources.assessment: The conclusion restates the achieved two-dimensional diffraction control by launch tilt. There is no concrete future experiment or unresolved question. The immediately preceding paragraph already attributes asymmetric shape at one zero-quadratic-diffraction direction to remaining cubic diffraction.

sources.title: Nonlinear Effects in Waveguide Arrays
sources.author: Hagai Eisenberg
read_locations: PDF p.43, printed p.38, Section 3.3, Eqs.3.4-3.5 and following paragraph
sources.author_explicit_unperformed_question: The author proposes engineering arbitrary periodic diffraction by composing segments with different cosine harmonics, and gives a triangular-dispersion target and a two-array approximation. This is a concrete proposal rather than a question stated in a conclusion.
short_quotes: any arbitrary periodic function can be spanned by its sine and cosine Fourier elements
only two directions while experiencing no diffraction
sources.completed_in_same_work: The following experiment uses otherwise identical equal-length sections with alternating tilt to demonstrate reduced, zero and anomalous average diffraction. It does not demonstrate the arbitrary triangular-band target proposed in the preceding paragraph.
sources.scope_limit: The proposed piecewise optical arrays are not automatically equivalent to static long-range exchange in a magnet. A Fourier-harmonic Hamiltonian is a transferable toy-model implementation.

followup_checks.title: Long-range interaction in waveguide lattices
followup_checks.read_scope: Official APS abstract and bibliographic record; full text not obtained in this branch.
followup_checks.relevance: Official abstract already describes general two-dimensional long-range coupling and engineered diffraction-free possibilities. Thus adding distant neighbors or claiming general band engineering is not novel.

followup_checks.title: Waveguide Arrays: Interaction to Many Neighbors
followup_checks.read_scope: Publisher-indexed full text excerpts including model examples and complete Section 5 Conclusions; direct web open returned HTTP429.
followup_checks.relevance: Analytical general long-range propagator and illustrative first-through-fourth-neighbor cases already exist. Its conclusion does not add a specific future-work promise.

followup_checks.title: Waveguide Arrays Interaction to Second Neighbors: Semi-Infinite Case
followup_checks.read_scope: Publisher-indexed introduction and abstract; direct page opening failed.
followup_checks.author_future_statement_paraphrase: Extending the paraxial formalism to explicit nonparaxial corrections is named as future research.
followup_checks.assessment: This is an explicit recent future direction, but it changes the optical propagation approximation and is poorly matched to the present single-magnon lattice problem. Not recommended as a minimal demo for this project.

followup_checks.title: On-chip arbitrary dispersion engineering with deep photonic networks
followup_checks.assessment: Experimental triangular group-delay-dispersion versus wavelength in Mach-Zehnder networks is not the triangular Bloch dispersion versus wavevector of the thesis proposal. It cannot establish that exact proposal solved.

queries: "Discrete solitons in nonlinear zigzag optical waveguide arrays with tailored diffraction properties"
selection: Do not promote Longhi2009 or Chen2007 to author-explicit open questions. Harmonic band engineering is a feasible benchmark-inspired toy demo, not an established novel project; prioritize newer explicit gaps if other branches provide them.
coverage_limit: Bounded primary-source search through 2026-10-21. Not finding an exact 1/27 Gaussian-lifetime example does not prove novelty. No simulations performed in this branch.
